{{More citations needed|date=July 2023}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{use mdy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox television season | bgcolor = #FFBF45 | image = dwts10poster.jpg | caption = Promotional poster, featuring former pro dancers [[Edyta Śliwińska]] and [[Alec Mazo]] | module1 = {{Infobox reality competition season | host = {{Plainlist| * [[Tom Bergeron]] * [[Brooke Burke]] }} | judges = {{Plainlist| * [[Carrie Ann Inaba]] * [[Len Goodman]] * [[Bruno Tonioli]] }} | celebrity_winner = [[Nicole Scherzinger]] | professional_winner = [[Derek Hough]] }} | num_episodes = 19 | network = [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] | first_aired = {{start date|2010|3|22}} | last_aired = {{end date|2010|5|25}} }} '''Season ten''' of ''[[Dancing with the Stars (American TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]]'' premiered on March 22, 2010, on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] network. [[The Pussycat Dolls]] singer [[Nicole Scherzinger]] and [[Derek Hough]] won the competition, while Olympic figure skater [[Evan Lysacek]] and [[Anna Trebunskaya]] finished second, and ESPN host [[Erin Andrews]] and [[Maksim Chmerkovskiy]] finished third.{{Cite web|url = https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/nicole-scherzinger-wins-dancing-with-the-stars/|title = Nicole Scherzinger Wins 'Dancing With the Stars'|date = 2014-05-25|access-date = 2014-07-13|website = |publisher = Fox News|archive-date = December 21, 2024|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20241221181120/https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/nicole-scherzinger-wins-dancing-with-the-stars/|url-status = live}} ==Cast== ===Couples=== This season featured eleven celebrity contestants. [[Damian Whitewood]], from the Broadway dance revue ''Burn the Floor'', joined the cast of professionals this season. {{small|on May 25, 2010}} |} ;Future appearances Pamela Anderson returned for the [[Dancing with the Stars (American season 15)|All-Stars]] season, where she was paired with [[Tristan MacManus]]. ===Host and judges=== [[Samantha Harris]] did not return as co-host for this season due to her commitments on ''[[The Insider (TV series)|The Insider]]'' and ''[[Entertainment Tonight]]''. On March 8, 2010, [[Tom Bergeron]] announced on ''[[Good Morning America]]'' that his new co-host would be [[Dancing with the Stars (American season 7)|season seven]] champion [[Brooke Burke]]. [[Len Goodman]], [[Carrie Ann Inaba]], and [[Bruno Tonioli]] all returned as judges. ==Scoring chart== The highest score each week is indicated in {{fontcolor|#004600|'''bold green'''}} with a dagger ({{dagger}}), while the lowest score each week is indicated in {{fontcolor|#800000|''italicized red''}} with a double-dagger ({{double-dagger}}).
